question:
A 64-year-old male is evaluated at his primary care physician's office, accompanied by his spouse, for
tremors that have been present for approximately one month. The tremor is isolated to his right hand
and becomes more pronounced during television viewing. His wife reports noticing a slowdown in his
movements, particularly evident in his walking pattern over recent weeks. He has a history of recent
consultation with a headache specialist for worsening migraines with associated nausea and vomiting,
for which he received treatment. The patient has no other medical conditions. Physical examination
reveals increased resistance during passive movement of the upper extremities. His walking pattern
demonstrates instability, mild leg dragging, and shortened steps when walking a short distance. What
is the most probable underlying cause of this patient's clinical presentation? Answer Choices: (A)
D2-receptor antagonism (B) Cerebellar degeneration (C) Overactivity of the subthalamic nucleus (D)
Peripheral neuropathy affecting motor control (E) Ischemic stroke affecting the corticospinal tract (F)

Increased GABAergic output from the basal ganglia (G) Lacunar infarcts in the basal ganglia (H)
Neuronal loss in the substantia nigra pars compacta (I) Reduced dopamine synthesis in the striatum (J)
Autoimmune-mediated destruction of the basal ganglia
 A. Reduced dopamine synthesis in the striatum
B. Cerebellar degeneration
C. Lacunar infarcts in the basal ganglia
D. Increased GABAergic output from the basal ganglia
E. Neuronal loss in the substantia nigra pars compacta
F. D2-receptor antagonism
G. Autoimmune-mediated destruction of the basal ganglia
H. Ischemic stroke affecting the corticospinal tract
I. Peripheral neuropathy affecting motor control
J. Overactivity of the subthalamic nucleus
